gallery.title: File:Humaitá in S. Paraguay wetlands.jpg
gallery.credit: Own work
gallery.description:
The fortress of Humaitá in the wetlands of southern Paraguay.
The fortress was on a tight bend on the river Paraguay.  At the bottom of the map the river debouches into the river Paraná, the boundary with Argentina.  Notice the 3 km scale.  Base map in Schneider (1872: Berlin), "Der Krieg der Triple-Allianz", volume I.

gallery.title: File:López curupayty trench.jpg
gallery.artist: Museo Histórico Nacional, unidentified photographer; Cándido López (1840-1902)
gallery.credit: 'Cándido López' ed. Fermín Fevre, Editorial El Ateneo (Buenos Aires: 2000), scan and crop
gallery.description: A detail from the Argentine painter's oil on canvas depicting the Paraguayan trench at the Battle of Curupayty (22 September 1866).  Pouring out a hail of grape and canister shot from a hastily erected earthwork, the Paraguayans inflicted the worst defeat the Allies (Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay) ever sustained.

gallery.title: File:Garmendia Paraguayan sentry.jpg
gallery.credit: Marcela F. Garrido, 'José Ignacio Garmendia', Historia Visual, Museo Roca, Buenos Aires, 2011
gallery.description: Paraguayan sentry in the War of the Triple Alliance, by the Argentine general and amateur watercolourist José Ignacio Garmendia.  Paraguayans fought fiercely and their courage was admired by their enemies.

gallery.title: File:Humaitá flanking concept.jpg
gallery.credit: Own work
gallery.description: This map, which is an annotated version of the public domain map 'Atlas Historico da Guerra do Paraguay", Plates 4 and 5, by E.C. Jourdan of  the corps of engineers of the Brazilian army (Rio de Janeiro: 1871) shows the concept of the Mitre/Caixas flanking plan by which the fortress would be encircled and cut off by land.  On the left is the River Paraguay; the fortress blocks its navigation.

gallery.title: File:Paraguayans plundering Tuyutí.jpg
gallery.credit: Marcela F. Garrido, 'José Ignacio Garmendia', Historia Visual, Museo Roca, Buenos Aires, 2011
gallery.description: Paraguayan soldiers looting the Allied camp at the second battle of Tuyutí, 3 November 1867.  The flags (Swiss, French, etc) denote the nationalities of the sutlers' stores that catered for the allied soldiery, and where almost anything could be bought, at a price.

gallery.title: File:Guardia on the River Paraguay.jpg
gallery.credit: Marcela F. Garrido, 'José Ignacio Garmendia', Historia Visual, Museo Roca, Buenos Aires, 2011
gallery.description: A guardia (lookout point) on the River Paraguay during the War of the Triple Alliance.  There are thatched buildings for the garrison, a mangrullo (watchtower), and on the river a steam vessel ia moored.  These installations were traditional in Paraguay. By the Argentine general and amateur watercolourist José Ignacio Garmendia.

gallery.title: File:Argentine officers around campfire.jpg

gallery.description: Argentine officers around the campfire

gallery.title: File:Italian band in Paraguayan War.jpg
gallery.credit: 'Álbum de retratos e vistas referentes ao Paraguai', National Library of Brazil
gallery.description: A band of Italian revolutionaries fighting in the Argentine army during the Paraguayan War.  These men, comrades of Garibaldi, fled Italy to South America and after many adventures are photographed at Tuyu-Cué in the wetlands of southern Paraguay.  Their colonel is Pipo Giribone (seated, right foreground).  This photograph must have been taken before early 1868, when Giribone was killed in a Paraguayan ambush.  The musicians (white headger) may have doubled as fighting men and certainly had the task of removing the wounded from battlefields.

gallery.title: File:Estabelecimento novo.jpg
gallery.credit: Own work
gallery.description: In the Paraguayan War, the outwork or redoubt called "Estabelecimento Novo" by the Brazilians ("Cierva" by the Paraguayans).  This map shows that the outwork was not on the River Paraguay, as the Allies had thought, but on the shore of an inland lagoon.  It had no strategic value; it was a bluff.  Its hard-fought capture on 19 February 1868 with serious loss of life turned out to be pointless.  (Base map by E.C. Jourdan of the Brazilian engineering corps, about 1870.)

gallery.title: File:Confluence and Humaitá.jpg
gallery.artist: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center from Greenbelt, MD, USA
gallery.credit: Paraguay
gallery.description:
Confluence of the rivers Paraguay (above) and Paraná (center).  This image from space, created by the Goddard Space Flight Center, has been annotated by User:Ttocserp to show the site of the Fortress of Humaitá during the Paraguayan War.  The Chaco was then in dispute between Paraguay and Argentina.

gallery.title: File:Profile at Paso Gómez.png
gallery.credit: Own work
gallery.description:
An earthwork profile as used by the Paraguayan forces at the fortress of Humaitá.  Artillery on wooden platforms (not shown) fired grape or canister i.e. towards the right.   The surface was usually revetted with turf sods.
This is a a cropped and annotated version of Plate V of George Thompson's "The War in Paraguay" (1869).
